message.content: {"title":"Population & Property Dynamics","narrative":"The model tracks three populations—susceptible, infected, and recovered—across a 50×50 toroidal grid of 200 agents. Infection occurs through proximity, and after a fixed infection_timer the infected transition to recovered, conferring immunity. Although the exact time series counts are not provided, the simulation is designed to run until no infected agents remain. Thus, over time we expect the susceptible count to decline as infections spread, the infected count to rise to a peak then fall to zero, and the recovered count to increase monotonically until it plateaus at its final value.","key_findings":[],"causal_links":[],"emergent_phenomena":["Disease‐free equilibrium reached after all infected agents recover, demonstrating herd immunity emergent at the population level once infection runs its course."]}
